I hit the tool budget mid-build, so here's where things stand and what's still in my hands rather than yours.

Your three observations
1. Adam and Betty can't change their display names — a miss, not a design choice. §4.6 of REQUIREMENTS specifies a profile page for every person ("manage credentials… phone number and/or email address… postal addresses"), and §11.1 of the spec repeats it. But the profile page never got assigned to a milestone — M2 was "identity," M3 was "tables & joining," and the profile surface fell in the crack between them. What exists today is a scattered set of credential pages (/account/passkeys, /account/enroll-totp) with no hub and no way to edit the three self-owned fields. The person table has had display_name, email_address, and phone_number since 0001, and DapperUserStore.UpdateAsync already persists all three — there was simply no surface calling it.

This matters more than cosmetics for what's coming next: §11.2 groups the kitchen queue by table label → person display name → order. Walking into M4 with staff who can't set their own display names would mean kitchen tickets reading betty instead of Betty.

2. The checkboxes — a real CSS defect, and I found the exact cause. app.css has .form-field input { width: 100%; padding: 0.6rem 0.75rem; border-radius: 8px }. CreateStaff.razor puts class="form-field roles-fieldset" on the fieldset, so every <InputCheckbox> inside inherits it and stretches to the full panel width. Worse, the page's inline .role-option { display: flex } loses on specificity to .form-field label (0,1,1 vs 0,1,0), so the label goes back to display: block and the text drops below the stretched box. That's precisely the "not aligned to anything" you saw. Fix is an input[type="checkbox"] override plus a shared .choice-list .choice pattern with enough specificity to win.

3. Booth 1, the rotating QR, and the reconnect loop — all working as specified. The Reconnecting… behaviour is display.js measuring staleness from when the script saw the refresh token change rather than a server timestamp, which is why it survives a kiosk with a wrong clock.

What I built before running out of tools
Complete and staged: ProfileDetails.cs (pure normalize/validate helper — trim, whitespace collapse, control-character stripping, loose email/phone shape checks, SameAs for no-op detection), Profile.razor at /account, ChangePassword.razor at /account/change-password (both branches — change and first-time add), and ProfileDetailsTests.cs (16 pure facts/theories).

I verified against dotnet/aspnetcore release/10.0 source rather than memory: UpdatePasswordHash rotates the security stamp inside both ChangePasswordAsync and AddPasswordAsync, so both paths need RefreshSignInAsync or the person signs themselves out; UpdateUserAsync does not rotate it, which is correct for a display-name edit.

Still to do — the surgical edits to existing files, plus the tarball: AccountRoutes (two constants), MainLayout.razor (collapse "Security" + "Passkeys" into one "Account" link, which also relieves the 375px header), app.css (checkbox fix + profile styles), CreateStaff.razor (shared choice classes, drop the inline <style>), and the doc set (REQUIREMENTS §4.6, spec §11.1 + a new §11.6, an F-35 ledger row, BUILD_PROGRESS).

I have an extractor that pulls every file out of dump.txt and checks it against its recorded SHA-256 (192/194 exact), so those edits will be applied programmatically to the real current text — no retyping, no drift.

No files to delete in this slice. Say continue and I'll finish the edits and hand you the .tar.gz.

What's in it

Changed (8) — ObligationsEnforcement.cs (two AccountRoutes constants), MainLayout.razor, CreateStaff.razor, app.css, and the four docs. Every one of these was extracted from dump.txt, SHA-256-verified against its recorded hash, and edited programmatically against exact anchors — no retyping, so the ~2,300 lines of doc text you already have come back byte-identical apart from the intended inserts.

Things worth knowing before you build
/account/change-password and /account/change-password-required are distinct routes, and IsExemptPath uses StartsWithSegments, which compares whole segments — so the voluntary page is correctly not exempt from the obligations pipeline. A staff member with must_change_password still gets the forced page.

UserManager.UpdateAsync doesn't rotate the security stamp (verified against release/10.0), so saving a display name won't cut live sessions. But UpdatePasswordHash does, on both the change and add paths — hence RefreshSignInAsync in CompleteAsync. If a password change bounces you to /sign-in, that refresh didn't fire.

Two .razor files are the likely compiler-catch sites, as usual. Profile.razor uses IList<string> _roles = [] (collection expression targeting the interface) and UserManager.GetPasskeysAsync, matching what Passkeys.razor already does.

The CSS fix also made .form-actions a wrapping flex row with a gap — that quietly improves several existing pages where a primary button and a "Cancel" link were butting together, so expect small spacing changes beyond the staff-creation form. Worth a glance at 375px.

Docs
REQUIREMENTS.md §4.6 now states display-name editing and username immutability outright and records that the three fields are the person's own. TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md §11.1 points at a new §11.6 /account; §19's M2 line names the profile page and admits it landed after M3. DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md gains F-35. Addresses stay unsurfaced, with the reason recorded in §11.6 — nothing in v1 consumes an address, and a form for data no reader exists for is scaffolding pretending to be a feature.

Still deferred from M2, untouched: voluntary TOTP removal plus the §4.2 self-removal rule, the grant-time passkey mandate for kitchen/administrator, and guest self-registration on the join path.

Next is M4 — ordering. Living order and the §6.6 locking protocol, staging UI, batch send with all-or-nothing validation, fulfillment/reversal, fold-equivalence tests, kitchen surface. Confirm this builds green first — M4 is the milestone you least want to enter on an unverified tree.
